title: After all that care, every one of you will die.
subtitle: The stage nobody skips
then: Right after the wonder of creation, the verse says plainly: {idea}after that, you will die.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says after first being created from nothing, {trap}you will eventually die.{/trap} The same Creator who brought you through each stage brings you through this one.
now: A funeral prayer after Jumu'ah. You stand in the row, then go back to your car and check your messages. {idea}The verse wants that moment to last a little longer.{/idea}
old: Death is far off. I will think about it later.
new: Death is the next stage in a story Allah has written with care.
try: Spend two quiet minutes today thinking about what you would want to have done if today were the last.

title: Then you will be raised again.
subtitle: The creation of the Hereafter
then: Ibn Kathir says you will be {idea}created anew{/idea}, souls returned to bodies, and all creation brought to account. {reward}If deeds are good, they are rewarded{/reward}; if bad, punished. The verse comes right after the stages of the womb as if to say: you saw what He can do.
now: You save drafts, back up photos, keep receipts in case you need them later. {idea}This verse says there is a later where your life will be opened again.{/idea} Everything you do today is being saved.
old: Once I am gone, it is all over.
new: The One who made me from nothing will raise me again, and my deeds will be there.
try: Do one good deed today that only Allah will see, and let it be saved for that Day.

title: Seven heavens above you, and none of you is unnoticed.
subtitle: The vast sky and a Creator who is never unaware
then: After man, Allah turns to the heavens, as He often pairs the two. Ibn Kathir says {idea}no heaven hides from Him another, no sea hides what is in its depths{/idea}. He knows what goes into the earth and what comes out, and {reward}He is with you wherever you are.{/reward}
now: Late at night, the city lights, a feeling that no one really sees what you carry. A huge sky and one small person on a balcony. {idea}The sky is vast, and still you are not missed.{/idea}
old: In a universe this big, nobody notices me.
new: The One who built the heavens is never unaware of me.
try: Step outside tonight, look up for one minute, and tell Allah one thing you have told no one.

title: Rain comes measured, and it could be taken away.
subtitle: Water you never had to earn
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah sends rain {reward}not so much it ruins the land, not so little it fails the crops{/reward}. He lists how it could be taken: no rain, sent to the wasteland, made salty, or sunk too deep to reach. {idea}But by His mercy it falls sweet and settles in the earth.{/idea}
now: You fill a glass from the tap without looking. You run the shower for ten minutes. {trap}A water cut in your area for one day and the whole street is in chaos.{/trap} {idea}Every glass is a gift kept in place.{/idea}
old: Water is a utility I pay a bill for.
new: Water is a measured mercy that could be taken any day.
try: Before your next drink of water, pause and say alhamdulillah slowly.

title: From that water, gardens and the fruit you eat.
subtitle: Dates and grapes, and every region's fruit

row.title: fruit
sub: to look at, wait for, eat

then: Dates and grapes were the gardens the people of the Hijaz knew. Ibn Kathir says {idea}the people of each region have fruits that are Allah's blessing to them{/idea}, for which they can never thank Him enough. You look at its beauty, wait for it to ripen, {reward}then eat.{/reward}
now: The mango in summer, the apples in autumn, the bowl of fruit on the kitchen counter that nobody notices until it goes brown. {idea}Your local fruit is your verse.{/idea}
old: Fruit is just something from the supermarket.
new: The fruit near me is a gift grown from rain Allah sent.
try: Eat one piece of fruit today slowly, and thank Allah for the rain behind it.

title: A tree from Sinai gives oil and food.
subtitle: The olive, from a blessed tree
then: Ibn Kathir says this is the olive tree, from the mountain where {idea}Allah spoke to Musa{/idea}, with olive trees around it. The Prophet ﷺ said: {reward}eat olive oil and apply it, for it comes from a blessed tree.{/reward}
now: The bottle of olive oil next to the stove. Bread dipped in it at breakfast with your family. {idea}The Quran pauses on the thing you reach for without thinking.{/idea}
old: Everyday food has nothing to do with faith.
new: Even my kitchen shelf holds signs of Allah's care.
try: At your next meal, name one ingredient and thank Allah for it by name.

title: In livestock there is a lesson, not only a meal.
subtitle: Milk, meat, wool, and much more

row.title: I bought it, it is mine

then: Ibn Kathir lists the gifts: {reward}milk that comes out pure from between dung and blood, meat, wool and hair, and their backs for riding{/reward}. He cites another verse that ends: {idea}will they not then be grateful?{/idea}
now: Milk in your coffee, a wool jumper in winter, a lamb dish at Eid. {idea}You did not design any of it.{/idea} A lesson is sitting on your plate every day.
old: Animals are just products in a shop.
new: Every animal that serves me is a lesson in gratitude.
try: Before your next meal with meat or milk, say bismillah and a short thank you.

title: On them and on ships, you are carried.
subtitle: Every journey rides on something given
then: The list of signs ends with travel. Ibn Kathir notes animals {reward}carry heavy loads to lands you could not reach except with great trouble{/reward}, and cites: {idea}your Lord is full of kindness, Most Merciful.{/idea} The verse then leads into the story of a ship: Nuh's.
now: The plane lands and people clap. The bus gets you to work on time. The car starts on a cold morning. {idea}You were carried again.{/idea}
new: Every journey I make, I am being carried by what Allah gave.
try: On your next trip, say the travel dua or simply: glory to the One who subjected this for us.

title: Nuh's whole message fits in one line.
subtitle: Worship Allah, you have no god but Him
then: The surah turns from signs in creation to the history of Prophets. Nuh came to {trap}warn his people of the punishment for associating partners with Allah{/trap}. His call was simple: {idea}worship Allah, you have no god but Him. Do you not fear Him?{/idea}
now: You give your fears and hopes to many things: the boss's mood, the bank balance, what people think. {idea}Nuh's question still lands: who do you really fear?{/idea}
old: I believe in Allah, so this message is not for me.
new: Worshipping Allah alone means taking back my heart from everything else I fear.
try: Notice one thing you feared today more than Allah. Hand it to Him in a short dua.

title: He is just a man like you, they said.
subtitle: The chiefs attack the messenger, not the message
then: The leaders did not answer Nuh's call. They attacked him: {trap}he is a human like you, he wants to make himself superior{/trap}. If Allah wanted a messenger He would send angels, and {trap}our forefathers never heard of this{/trap}.
now: Someone younger gives you good advice and you think, who is he to tell me? A colleague points out a mistake and you wonder about her motives. {idea}The question is not who said it, but whether it is true.{/idea}
old: I judge advice by who it comes from.
new: Truth can come through an ordinary person, and I should weigh it as truth.
try: Think of one piece of advice you dismissed because of who gave it. Reconsider it honestly.

title: Call him mad, then wait for him to go away.
subtitle: Labeling and waiting as a way to dodge truth
then: They called Nuh {trap}a man possessed by madness{/trap}. Ibn Kathir explains their plan: {trap}wait until he dies, put up with him until you are rid of him.{/trap} Not one argument against what he said.
now: The reminder you keep scrolling past. The friend who invites you to pray, whom you call "a bit extreme" and wait for them to stop. {idea}Waiting out a reminder does not make it go away.{/idea}
old: If I ignore it long enough, the reminder will stop.
new: Labeling a reminder is not the same as answering it.
try: Pick one reminder you have been waiting out, and take one small step on it today.

title: When they denied him, Nuh turned to his Lord.
subtitle: My Lord, help me
then: After long years of calling and being mocked, Nuh asked Allah: {idea}my Lord, help me, because they have denied me.{/idea} Another verse says he called: {trap}I have been overcome{/trap}, so help me.
now: You tried to do the right thing at work and got laughed at in the meeting. Your family dismissed your choice. {idea}Before you rant in the group chat, there is a shorter prayer: Rabbi unsurni.{/idea}
old: When people reject me, I must fight back or quit.
new: When people reject me, I can tell my Lord plainly and ask Him for help.
try: Next time you feel rejected, say quietly: My Lord, help me. Then wait before replying.

title: Build the ship under Our eyes.
subtitle: The answer to his prayer came as a task
then: Allah answered by telling Nuh to {idea}build a strong ship under His watch and guidance{/idea}, then take two of each kind and his family, except those already decreed, who did not believe. He was told {trap}not to plead for the wrongdoers{/trap}, for the decree was set.
now: You prayed for a way out of debt, and the answer looks like a budget spreadsheet and a second shift. {idea}Sometimes help comes as a task, with Allah watching you build.{/idea}
old: If Allah answers my dua, I should not have to work for it.
new: Often His answer is a task, and He watches over me while I do it.
try: Name one dua you have made and one practical step toward it. Take the step today.
